why.text: Schist terraces in mountain-sheltered valleys, with very cold winters and hot, dry summers, and many native grapes blended together.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, mostly blends; also sparkling wine and fortified Moscatel do Douro.

climate.text: Very cold winters, very hot dry summers; the Marão and Montemuro mountains block wet western winds. Mean annual temperatures run 11.8 to 16.5 °C.

soil.text: Mostly schist, with patches of granite; terracing and deep ploughing reshape many soils.

tastes.text: Reds: mostly blends of native grapes, complex and rich. Whites: good aroma and complexity, often fermented or aged in wood. Rosés: pink, aromatic, soft and sweet, lightly acidic.

styles.name: Moscatel do Douro
styles.text: Fortified white made only from Moscatel Galego Branco, 16.5 to 22% alcohol.

styles.name: Espumante
styles.text: Sparkling wine with second fermentation in bottle, some vintage ones need nine months in bottle.

styles.name: Colheita tardia
styles.text: Single-harvest wine where overripe grapes can be tasted.

why.text: Mild, wet Atlantic weather favours slow ripening and fresh acidity; the mostly granite soils give the whites their mineral notes.

styles.text: White, rosé and red wines, plus sparkling and quality sparkling; late-harvest wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Mild, without extreme heat or cold; about 1,200 mm of rain a year, irregular, with Atlantic winds through the river valleys.

soil.text: Shallow soils, mostly granite; two narrow strips of schist cross the region.

tastes.text: Whites: pale citrine, light and fruity or floral, to mineral and honeyed. Rosés: pale pink, red fruit. Reds: ruby to dark, wild fruits. Fresh, high acidity.

styles.name: Alvarinho (Monção e Melgaço)
styles.text: Subregion wines may name Alvarinho only here; optional term «Origem do Alvarinho».

styles.name: Espumante de Vinho Verde
styles.text: Sparkling wine, white, rosé or red, made from Vinho Verde base wine.

styles.name: Palhete / Palheto
styles.text: Red wine with up to 15% white grapes; the term is mandatory.

styles.name: Vindima Tardia
styles.text: Late-harvest wine from overripe grapes; honey and dried fruit aromas, sweet.
